clue.text: Cup drunk, alcoholic, round end of marriage, traditionally encouraged

indicators.note: a drunk cup is a wobbly, disordered one, so its three letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the strong-drink word goes round the final letter, holding it inside

parts.note: hard drinks are alcoholic ones, as in hard liquor

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A drinker's cup, a boozy toast and a marriage ending in the old way that people were cheered on.
explanation.walkthrough: UPCHEARD is Spenser's spelling of 'upcheered', hence 'traditionally'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upcheer is an archaic verb meaning to cheer up or hearten, and its past tense is used here.

clue.text: Husband occupying seat in church — that's a relief

indicators.note: the husband letter occupies the church seat, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pew is a church bench

explanation.surface: Husband finally takes his place in church, to everyone's relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is an exclamation of relief, said on escaping something unpleasant.

clue.text: Outcry in the US, Democrats all upset — slated with this?

indicators.note: the answer together with the word slated makes up the jumbled letters, so slated is set aside

parts.note: an anagram of these twelve letters, upset meaning knocked into a new order, which holds both the answer and the word slated
taken as written, the part of the jumble that is not the answer

explanation.surface: American protests as Democrats are all upset at being criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus SLATED shares its letters with DEMOCRATS ALL. CLAMOR is the American spelling, hence 'in the US'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamor is a loud public protest or demand, spelt this way in American English.

clue.text: Bible brought in, pawned, vandalized

indicators.note: the Bible letters are brought into the pawning word

parts.note: hocked is slang for pawned
AV is the Authorized Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible taken to the pawnshop and then defaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To havock (havoc) is to lay waste or devastate, so havocked means ravaged or wrecked.

clue.text: Horrified as before at having to limit fuel

indicators.note: at limits the fuel by sitting either side of it

parts.note: taken as written
gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Shocked, as before, at being made to ration fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Agast is an obsolete spelling of aghast, hence 'as before'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with horror or amazement; agast is the older spelling of it.

clue.text: Monarch retaining doctor as potato-peeler

indicators.note: the monarch keeps hold of the doctor, containing it

parts.note: a monarch is a ruler
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A king keeps a physician on as his potato-peeler.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumbler is a rotating drum machine that peels potatoes by tumbling them against an abrasive lining.

clue.text: Sold drugs, vile trade involving change of hands?

indicators.note: vile, in its debased form, the letters are corrupted into a new order
right is swapped for left, both being hands, so R becomes L

parts.note: taken as written before the swap

explanation.surface: Pushing drugs is a vile trade where things change hands.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left, the two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal drugs is to sell them illegally, so dealt is the past tense of that trade.

clue.text: Traditional volumes found among faded daybooks

indicators.note: the letters are tucked away among those of the next two words, running across the gap

parts.note: the hiding place

explanation.surface: Old traditional books turn up in a pile of faded diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are the two medieval Icelandic collections of Norse myth and poetry, volumes of traditional lore.

clue.text: In the manner of noodles, soft, wrapped in paper napkin

definitions.note: noodle is slang for a fool, so this means foolishly

indicators.note: the soft letter is wrapped inside the napkin

parts.note: a doily is a small ornamental paper mat or napkin
p, piano, is soft in music

explanation.surface: Noodles served softly in a paper napkin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noodles' looks like pasta, but a noodle is a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopily means stupidly or dozily, the way a noodle, an idiot, behaves.

clue.text: Tea maid's prepared for natural gap

indicators.note: prepared means made up afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: The maid's tea is ready to fill a natural break.
explanation.definitionFit: A diastema is a natural space between teeth, such as the gap between front teeth.

clue.text: Latin bird in part of choir producing jaunty movements

indicators.note: the Latin letter and the bird go in the choir section

parts.note: the altos are a section of a choir
an egret is a heron

explanation.surface: A Latin-singing bird among the choir's altos produces lively music.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegrettos are musical pieces or passages in a fairly brisk, light tempo.

clue.text: Intermittent

definitions.meaning: surface reading: occurring now and then, in fits and starts; setter's reading: the bare definition, since this is the word solvers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle prints only a definition, and entrants submit their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodical, a longer form of spasmodic, describes something coming in sudden fits rather than steadily.

clue.text: Romance of a kind getting Dougie all excited, name secreted (10, two words, apostrophe)

definitions.note: Romance here is a language family descended from Latin

indicators.note: something secreted is hidden away inside, so the name letter is tucked within the jumble
excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A love affair gets a man called Dougie thoroughly worked up, with a name kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romance' looks like a love affair but means a Romance language; langue d'oïl is the medieval French of northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Langue d'oïl is the group of northern French dialects, one of the Romance tongues descended from Latin.

clue.text: It helps to shift log rolling certainly round Virginia

indicators.note: rolling turns the built word over so it reads backwards, apt beside a log
the word for certainly goes round the state abbreviation

parts.note: yep is a casual yes
VA is the US postal abbreviation for the state

explanation.surface: A tool for shifting logs as they roll, in Virginia of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log rolling' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'log' and 'rolling' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A peavy (or peavey) is a lumberjack's lever with a spike and hinged hook, used for turning and moving logs.

clue.text: Dismay shown by the old man turning on mate

indicators.note: the reversed father sits on, that is before, the friend
turning the fatherly word round makes it read backwards

parts.note: the old man is slang for one's father, pa
a pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Father rounds on his friend, and the result is dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill someone with horror or consternation, a verb sense of the word dismay.

clue.text: Woman mostly in a bad way comes to us for charitable relief

indicators.note: the jumble arrives at the next piece, which follows it
letters in a bad way are in poor order, so they are rearranged
most of the word, dropping its final letter

parts.note: only the first four letters are used
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman who is down on her luck turns up asking us for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: AWMOUS is a Scots word for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, awmous means alms, money or food given to the poor as charity.

clue.text: Hardened clay, see, in grip of cold wind

indicators.note: held in the grip of the wind word, so put inside it

parts.note: the bise is a cold north wind in Switzerland and southern France
la is an old interjection meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Clay baked hard, you see, by the grip of a freezing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: BLAISE is a Scots word for hardened clay or shale, also spelt blaes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise, or blaes, is Scots for hardened clay or soft shale, used crushed for sports pitches.

clue.text: Polar vehicle? Steer from the rear, perched outside

indicators.note: the word for perched goes outside, around the other piece

parts.note: to have perched is to have sat

indicators.note: read from the rear, the steering word runs backwards

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering

explanation.surface: Driving a polar vehicle, you steer from the back while perched on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sno-Cat is a tracked vehicle built for travel over snow and ice, as on polar expeditions.

clue.text: Headlong fall? Nothing to ease the pain at cut

indicators.note: the little word is cut out of the phrase

parts.note: no means none, nothing
a sedative soothes pain
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: After a headlong tumble there is nothing to dull the pain of a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep downward plunge, as of an aircraft heading nose first.

clue.text: Horlicks (more than one) — or Bells?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: horlicks is British slang for a mess-up, and in the plural these are blunders
second meaning: bells are things that clang

explanation.walkthrough: Horlicks is a British malted bedtime drink whose name is also slang for a botch; 'Bells' looks like the whisky brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangers are glaring blunders in British slang, and literally things that make a clang.

clue.text: One manipulates accounts to mislead key filter somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some other order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Somebody rigging the books manages to mislead, somehow, using a key filter.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite-flyer passes or raises money on dud cheques or bills, a fraudster who tricks with accommodation paper.

clue.text: Like a long run? Men should be dressed in a hat

definitions.note: an adjective, describing a race of that distance

indicators.note: the jumbled men go inside the hat

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

indicators.note: dressed, set in order differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Men ought to wear a hat on a lengthy run.
explanation.walkthrough: A tile is old slang for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-mile race is a long-distance run, so ten-mile describes such a run's length.

clue.text: They emit foul smell — very large gauge reverse of ideal

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing size
a meter is a measuring gauge

indicators.note: the ideal word is written in reverse order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; its 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A measuring device that is huge and far from perfect gives off a stink.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 reversed is 1A, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmeteria are forked glands that swallowtail caterpillars push out to release a repellent odour, plural of osmeterium.

clue.text: Sectarian, fatuous by the sound of it

indicators.note: the answer is said the same as the word for fatuous

parts.note: moony means dreamily silly

explanation.surface: Calling a sect member fatuous, judging by how they come across.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moonie is a member of the Unification Church, the sect founded by Sun Myung Moon.

clue.text: Dog or kitten mostly excluded round small cooking area

indicators.note: the shortened kitten is taken away from all round the answer, leaving only the middle

parts.note: a kitchenette is a small kitchen
kitten minus its last letter gives five letters; the first three are taken from the front of the kitchen word and the last two from its end

explanation.surface: Keeping a dog or kitten out of the kitchenette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' means a firedog, not a pet: a chenet is an andiron.
explanation.definitionFit: A chenet is a firedog or andiron, the metal support for logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Maori settlement dividing street up for NZ shrubs

indicators.note: the Maori word splits the street letters
in a down clue, up means read bottom to top

parts.note: utu is the Maori notion of settlement or recompense

explanation.surface: A Maori village splits the street, with New Zealand bushes planted along it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' looks like a village; utu is Maori for satisfaction or the settling of a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutu is a New Zealand shrub of the genus Coriaria with poisonous berries.

clue.text: One's produced in boiling haunts?

indicators.note: boiling letters seethe and come out in a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Something that turns up in sweltering resorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: hot holiday haunts are where you'd put one on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunhat is the headgear brought out in baking-hot places, shading its wearer from the fierce sun.

clue.text: Theological student, one of two for tutor occupying comfy seat

indicators.note: the letter occupies the seat, sitting inside it

parts.note: a sofa is a comfortable seat
tutor contains two Ts, and one is taken

explanation.surface: A divinity student sits with his tutor on a comfy sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A softa is a Muslim student of theology and sacred law, a seminary pupil.

clue.text: Logical fallacy I mould deviously

indicators.note: deviously, by a roundabout route, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A philosopher confesses to shaping a misleading argument by underhand means.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolum, in Bacon's sense, is an idol of the mind: a false notion or fallacy distorting reasoning.

clue.text: Syrup, golden stuff, grand to have for breakfast?

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: Golden syrup and a grand helping of it to have at breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgeat is a sweet syrup flavoured with almonds and orange-flower water, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Chopper making my heart shift?

indicators.note: the two middle letters of the name, its heart, slide one place to the right past the last letter

parts.note: the setter's own name stands for my, since Azed is writing the clue

explanation.surface: A tool that sets the pulse racing, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the setter speaking: Azed's name, with its middle pair moved to the end, makes the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade set at right angles to the handle, used for shaping wood.

clue.text: Supreme commander has little time, once surrounded

parts.note: C-in-C is commander-in-chief
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A top commander has little time, having once been encircled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinct is an obsolete word meaning girded or encircled, hence the 'once' signalling archaic usage.

clue.text: Ritual sword play to culminate in final strike

indicators.note: the word for culminate goes in the final-strike letters

parts.note: KO is a knockout, the blow that ends a fight
to culminate is to end

explanation.surface: A ceremonial sword bout builds to its climax in the deciding blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords, practised with formal etiquette.

clue.text: A large bird I see nesting — successful result of this?

definitions.text: A large bird I see nesting — successful result of this?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nesting puts the two little pieces inside the bird

parts.note: a vulture is a large bird of prey
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like the word see

explanation.surface: Spotting a big bird settling on its nest is the reward of a breeder's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a large bird nesting is what successful bird-rearing produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviculture is the keeping and breeding of birds, whose success shows when captive birds nest.

clue.text: Language of the Net, fast if not fine

indicators.note: the word for fast is taken without the fine letter

parts.note: fleet means swift

explanation.surface: Online slang is quick, if not elegant.
explanation.definitionFit: Leet, or leetspeak, is an internet jargon replacing letters with digits and symbols, used by gamers and hackers.

clue.text: Rate mess appalling in sewer

indicators.note: an appalling mess is a dreadful muddle, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The amount of filth in a drain is shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A seamster is a person who sews seams, a tailor or needleworker.
